entries.d: Who art thou, O great mountain? before Zerubbabel thou shalt become a plain: and he shall bring forth the headstone thereof with shoutings, crying, Grace, grace unto it. The setting is the rebuilding of the temple by a discouraged remnant, and the headstone is the last stone laid

To make whole — physically, spiritually, relationally. Christ’s healings demonstrated kingdom-arrival (Matt 11:5); the church is to pray for the sick (James 5:14); ultimate healing is bodily resurrection. The healer is YHWH-Rapha (Exod 15:26).

entries.d: The word appears in a strange place. Isaiah is describing the collapse of Judah, when the state is so broken that men will grab a brother in the street and say, thou hast clothing, be thou our ruler — and the brother will swear in that day, I will not be an healer; for in my hous

In Old Testament law, leprosy required ceremonial isolation; the leper was unclean and dwelt outside the camp (Lev 13). Cleansing of leprosy was so rare that 2 Kings 5:7 records the king of Israel tearing his clothes when asked to heal Naaman. Christ's healing of leprosy was ther

entries.p: n. pl. (those who hear, especially the word preached; rendering Greek akroates

The heart in Scripture is the totality of the inner person — the seat of thought, will, desire, conscience, and spiritual orientation. It is not primarily the emotions (as in modern usage) but the command center of a human being. What the heart loves determines what the whole per
An anxious heart is one fragmented by worry, pulled in many directions at once. Paul prescribes the cure: prayer, supplication, thanksgiving, and the peace of God that surpasses understanding.

A bold heart speaks the gospel without shrinking. The Greek parresia (boldness, frankness, plain-speech) names both the disposition and the outward speech that flows from it. Acts 4:13 captures the apostolic example: Now when they saw the boldness of Peter and John, and perceived
A courageous heart is the obedient heart anchored in God's presence. Joshua receives the command three times: be strong and of a good courage, for the LORD thy God is with thee.

The native condition of the human heart since the fall: deceitful above all things and desperately wicked. It deceives both its owner and its observers; only God searches it, and only God can cure it.
A fearful heart in the bad sense is the spirit of cowardice, timidity that paralyzes obedience. Paul tells Timothy that God has not given this spirit, but power, love, and a sound mind.
A grateful heart is the ruled heart, governed by the peace of Christ and overflowing in thanksgiving. Colossians commands it as the standard posture of the redeemed.
A hard heart is one calloused by sin, deaf to God's voice, and unwilling to repent. Hebrews warns the church not to harden their hearts as Israel did in the wilderness.

A hardened heart is a heart that has become progressively resistant to the truth of God through repeated rejection, willful disobedience, or prolonged exposure to sin without repentance. Pharaoh is the supreme example: Scripture says both that Pharaoh hardened his own heart and t
A meek heart is the third Beatitude: blessed are the meek for they shall inherit the earth. Meekness is not weakness but strength tamed by God, the temper of the righteous king.

A soft heart is the gift of the new covenant, promised in Ezekiel as the heart of flesh replacing the heart of stone. It feels conviction, receives the Word, and turns toward God.

The heart God Himself unites, that fears His name without rival, walks in His truth without compromise, and is wholly His. It is David's prayer in Psalm 86:11 and the answer to the divided heart of Hosea 10:2.

David's covenant name for YHWH in Psalm 23: "The LORD is my shepherd; I shall not want." The shepherding image is foundational across Scripture — YHWH leads, feeds, protects, restores, and accompanies through the valley. Christ takes up the title in John 10: "I am the good shephe

The most-frequent compound divine name — "the LORD of hosts" or "LORD of armies." The hosts are angelic armies, celestial bodies, and the assembled people. YHWH commands the armies of heaven; nothing is outside His command. "The LORD of hosts is with us; the God of Jacob is our r

A yielding spirit is the settled inner posture of giving way — not breaking, but bending; not surrendering ground to evil, but surrendering self-will to God. Ecclesiastes commends it; Romans makes it the daily logic of being a living sacrifice.

The Hebrew word for fear, especially "fear of the LORD." Not anxious dread but reverent awe leading to obedience. The beginning of wisdom (Prov 9:10), the first commandment of the Shema's love (Deut 6:5 implies it), and the disposition that recognizes God for who He is.

Hebrew yir'ah, fear / reverence / awe, particularly the yir'at YHWH (fear of the LORD), the central wisdom-theological concept of the OT and the foundational disposition of the godly creature toward his Creator. The fear of the LORD is the great theme of OT wisdom literature: the

The yoke in Scripture runs from bondage to blessing. Egyptian bondage was a yoke (Lev 26:13). Jeremiah wore an actual wooden yoke to symbolize Babylon's coming dominion (Jer 27-28). But the yoke is also Christ's invitation: "Take my yoke upon you, and learn from me, for I am gent

A yokefellow is one who labors under the same yoke as another — the partner pulling the load alongside, sharing the discipline, the pace, and the weight. Paul uses the word for a faithful co-laborer in the gospel; the picture also fits husband and wife, ministry team, and any cov

Declaration used to justify an impulsive, risky, or indulgent choice: "might as well, you only live once." Deployed before a splurge, a bad decision, a drunken dare, or a life-choice someone knows they'll regret. The phrase front-loads the excuse: the action follows.

The Spirit-wrought ardor that consumes the saint with passion for God's glory, His house, His name, and His people. Unlike fleshly fanaticism, godly zeal burns according to knowledge, is purified by Christ, and bears the fruit of good works.
